paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend: Jesus is in charge, and everybody on that shore knows it. The two men shout, “What do You want with us, Son of God?” (Matthew 8:29), and then the demons beg, “If You drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs.” (Matthew 8:31). Nobody argues with Him. Jesus says one word, “Go!” (Matthew 8:32), and that's the end of the discussion.

Now look at the part that stings. The whole town comes out to meet Jesus, and they beg Him to leave their region (Matthew 8:34). The text doesn't say why, so I won't guess. But I will tell you this: meeting Jesus and welcoming Jesus are two different things.

So here's why it matters to you. Jesus stepped onto a shore where the two men were “so violent that no one could pass that way.” (Matthew 8:28), and nothing there was too much for Him. That means nothing in your week is too big to bring to Him either. So when He shows up in your reading today, friend, don't be the town. Pull up a chair, because this is one Visitor you want to keep.
